_how: Hand verdicts from the coadd stamps (cache/p9/units/p9/stamps/), the half-pass S/N, the single-frame share and vetting.json. A slow track rate is not used as evidence: near-static injections at 300-1000 au are recovered on the slowest tracks too. 'unexplained peak' means no artefact explanation was found; it is never a candidate planet.

P9T02#1.why: Most likely noise. S/N 7.06 against this field's null maximum 6.80 (a 0.26 margin); of the 27 fields with any peak at S/N >= 7, about half would show a real peak above their own null maximum by chance. Flux 56 +- 8 uJy is below the field's 50% completeness flux (66 uJy). Both halves contribute (5.7 / 4.5), the coadd is a faint compact blob with no star residual, no Gaia source brighter than G 19.3 or CatWISE source brighter than W1 16.2 within 60 arcsec, and no JPL-catalogued body (V < 25) within 60 arcsec. Its best track implies 30-37 au (1.9 arcsec/h). Not followed up in another pass.

P9T05#1.why: Second half only (1.9 / 11.8); dipole in the coadd beside a G 10.5 / W1 9.2 star 22 arcsec away.

P9T09#1.why: First half only (25.2 / 0.0); ring around a masked core; G 8.2 star 33 arcsec away (a Gaia G < 16 star 2.8 px from the peak).

P9T10#1.why: Subtraction dipole in the coadd, 32 arcsec from a W1 7.8 / G 11.3 star.

P9T13#1.why: Masked saturated core with a dipole in the coadd; half-pass S/N lopsided (2.8 / 10.7).

P9T14#1.why: First half only (8.1 / 0.8); diffuse coadd 30 arcsec from a G 9.7 / W1 8.6 star.
